zh.topic_title: National security conviction shows ‘pursuing democracy is a crime,’ Tiananmen vigil activist says in mitigation hearing

en.topic_title: National security conviction shows ‘pursuing democracy is a crime,’ Tiananmen vigil activist says in mitigation hearing
en.topic_summary:
An activist who once organised annual vigils to commemorate the Tiananmen crackdown has said that a Hong Kong court’s decision to convict her under national security legislation amounts to saying that “pursuing democracy is a crime.”



The 2018 candlelight vigil commemorating the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown in Beijing. File photo: Kris Cheng/HKFP.



Chow Hang-tung was convicted last week, alongside Lee Cheuk-yan and Albert Ho, of inciting subversion under a Beijing-imposed national security law.
